KEY MESSAGE 1... 
Elevated heat risk will continue for one more day across Central and 
Northwestern Ohio today before temperatures begin to moderate Friday 
into the weekend. The ridge is slowly beginning to retreat to the 
southwest as low pressure moves north of the Great Lakes to the 
east. 850mb temperatures will still be around 20-22C for the western 
half of the CWA resulting in surface temperatures to be in the low 
90s. Dew points again will be elevated in the low to mid 70s that 
will push heat indices to around 100F this afternoon into the early 
evening. There's some uncertainty with the eastern extent of the 
elevated heat indices as precipitation is expected over the course 
of the day today. Current guidance suggests that precipitation will 
be scattered in Eastern Ohio through the morning and into the 
afternoon that will help keep heat indices down overall to the east. 
Whereas Western Ohio should be free of any scattered precipitation 
so temperatures will have the chance to climb before precipitation 
is expected in the early evening. By that time, more widespread
precipitation is expected to move in from the northwest that 
will temper heat indices this evening. Based on this, a Heat Advisory
has been issued for Central and Western Ohio for this afternoon
into the evening. Overnight, temperatures will still be warm 
with lows in the upper 60s to low 70s, though will not rise as 
much on Friday due to the rounds of precipitation expected 
throughout the day. A cold front will move south across the 
region late Friday into early Saturday and temperatures will 
regulate back to around seasonal for the weekend and into early 
next week. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
More rounds of thunderstorms and potential severe weather will 
continue through today and Friday and, to a lesser extent, 
Saturday morning. There will be isolated morning convection 
across the eastern portion of the CWA that should exit to the 
east with the shortwave. Another shortwave is expected to move 
into the region this afternoon/evening bringing support for more
thunderstorms and severe weather potential. Instability will 
still be elevated with MLCAPE around 1500-2000 J/kg and bulk 
shear of 30-35 knots. Lapse rates will also climb to around 
7.0-7.5 C/km with daytime heating. This will promote downburst 
potential across the region during the afternoon and evening for
any storms that start to develop. The better chance for showers
and thunderstorms will be in the later evening into the 
overnight with the shortwave. Clusters of thunderstorms are 
possible with this that will bring the threat for damaging wind 
gusts and large hail. An isolated tornado is possible as well as
0-1km shear vectors increase ahead of the feature. SPC has 
highlighted the entire area today in a Slight Risk (Level 2 out 
of 5) for severe weather due to this. The shortwave should exit 
to the southeast early Friday morning and a brief break is 
expected ahead of the next shortwave. 

This shortwave will enter the region from the northwest mid-morning 
Friday moving to the southeast. The ridge will have retreat to the 
southwest more by this time so the thunderstorm chances will have 
moved along with it to be more focused on the central and western 
portions of the CWA. There won't be much recover in the atmosphere 
between the previous shortwave and this one, so the severe weather 
threat will be lower. That being said, there will still be plenty of 
instability, especially in Central and Northwestern Ohio that will 
help support any severe weather. There's still some discrepancies 
among the models for Friday in regards to timing and coverage, but 
generally, coverage should be lower, limiting the overall severe 
weather impacts. A cold front will be associated with this shortwave 
as it pushes to the south through early Saturday. The front will be 
slow to move out of the area, so lingering showers and thunderstorms 
are possible into early Saturday morning.

In addition to the severe weather potential, there will be the 
chance for heavy rain and flooding in places that see persistent 
rainfall. With the elevated CAPE, PWATs will be around 1.50-2.00" 
across the region that will give enough support for the flooding 
potential. Generally, the time frame that looks to be the most 
susceptible to flooding will be tonight into Friday. 

KEY MESSAGE 3... 
High pressure will begin to build across the region Saturday 
afternoon and persist through early next week. Building south from 
Canada, this will drop high temperatures to a more pleasant upper 
70s to low 80s with lower humidity. Overnight lows will be down into 
the upper 50s to low 60s as well.
